plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing auctions you could have profitably won. With a value of $31, bidding exactly $31 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever profitable and never overpay.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could profitably win. With a value of $6, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly $6 regardless of what I expect others to bid.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy, regardless of others' actions. Since my private value is $0, winning the auction would mean paying some positive amount (the second-highest bid), which would result in a loss. Bidding my true value of $0 ensures I only win if the price is $0, avoiding any negative outcome. There's no incentive to bid higher since any win would cost more than the item is worth to me.
